meta.author: Dennis E. Taylor
notes: All summaries are original paraphrases written for this app.
firstBook = book where the entry first appears; hide entries with firstBook > reader's current book.
summary only covers what is known by the entry's firstBook. updates[] adds later developments, each tagged with its book, so the app can reveal them only once the reader gets there.
confidence: high = sources agree; medium = sources conflict or first-book tag is inferred (the later plausible book was chosen); low = book 6 premise only, from pre-release info.
related lists ids across terms, places and characters. Hide a related link when its target's firstBook is past the reader's book. Timeline events carry a book and an order within it.

when = in-universe year(s), from the fan-made Bobiverse wiki timeline (bobiverse.fandom.com/wiki/Timeline). A leading ~ marks an estimate: the exact event is not dated there, or (books 5-6) only the book's overall span is known.

books.title: We Are Legion (We Are Bob)
books.summary: A software engineer who froze his head wakes a century later as software, gets turned into an interstellar probe, and starts copying himself across nearby star systems.

books.title: For We Are Many
books.summary: The Bobs juggle evacuating a dying Earth, shepherding a primitive alien species, and the discovery of a planet-stripping alien civilization.

books.title: All These Worlds
books.summary: The war with the Others comes to a head, Earth's last survivors are moved to the stars, and the Bobs start seeing themselves as a new kind of species.

books.title: Heaven's River
books.summary: Over a century later, Bob tracks a long-lost clone to an enormous artificial habitat full of otter-like aliens, while the Bobiverse itself splits into feuding factions.

books.title: Not Till We Are Lost
books.summary: After the faction war, the Bobs face growing resentment, a new AI, wormhole experiments and an expedition to the galactic core that hints at why the galaxy seems so empty.

books.title: The Infinite Extent
books.summary: The Bobs dig into an ancient wormhole network and a derelict alien ship, look for a home for a large group of refugees, and face a threat on a galactic scale. (Audiobook 2026; hardcover listed for January 2027.)

terms.name: Replicant
terms.summary: A human mind scanned and run as software. Bob is one; so are the rival probes from other nations, and later some humans and aliens who choose to become one.

terms.name: Replicant matrix
terms.summary: The hardware that holds a replicant's mind. Losing the matrix means losing the person.

updates.text: Recovering a lost replicant's matrix becomes a key goal.

terms.name: HEAVEN Project
terms.summary: FAITH's program, run by its Ministry of Truth, to send replicant-run self-replicating probes out to find and claim habitable worlds. The name stands for Habitable Earths Abiogenic Vessel Exploration Network.

terms.name: Von Neumann probe
terms.summary: A spacecraft that mines resources at each new star, builds copies of itself and sends them onward. Every Bob is, technically, one of these.

terms.name: FAITH
terms.summary: The Free American Independent Theocratic Hegemony: the religious state that replaced the United States after a coup in 2041. In Bob's new century it runs most of North America and legally owns him as property.

terms.name: Brazilian Empire
terms.summary: A rival power with its own replicant probes. Its probes are aggressive and treat the Bobs as enemies.

terms.name: GUPPI / Guppy
terms.summary: The General Unit Primary Peripheral Interface: the semi-intelligent software between a replicant and his ship's systems. Bob gives it a fish-headed avatar and keeps upgrading it; it stays deadpan throughout the series.

terms.name: VR environment
terms.summary: Each Bob builds a virtual home to stay sane, usually a library with a fire, coffee, a butler and a cat. Their VR spaces drift apart as their personalities do.

terms.name: Replicative drift
terms.summary: Each copy of Bob comes out a little different from the one who made it. Over generations this adds up to very different personalities, and eventually to factions.

terms.name: SCUT
terms.summary: Bill and Garfield's faster-than-light radio (Subspace Communications Universal Transceiver). It reaches about 20 to 25 light years and turns the scattered Bobs into a real-time network; relays stretch it further.

terms.name: SUDDAR
terms.summary: Subspace Deformation Detection And Ranging: a subspace radar with a range of a few light minutes, far better than ordinary radar.

terms.name: SURGE drive
terms.summary: The reactionless drive (Subspace Reactionless Geotactic Emulation) the Bobs use to travel between stars, made practical by cheap fusion. Later variants also lift and move whole floating cities.

terms.name: Autofactory
terms.summary: Automated manufacturing that lets a Bob mine a system and build new ships, drones and copies without help.

terms.name: Cloaking
terms.summary: Stealth that makes Brazilian missiles invisible to SUDDAR, first met by the Bobs at 82 Eridani.

updates.text: Bill reverse-engineers it from captured Brazilian gear. In time the Bobs use it on their own weapons and ships.

terms.name: Bobiverse
terms.summary: The Bobs' half-joking name for their whole spread-out family of copies and the space they cover.

terms.name: Gorilloids
terms.summary: Large predators on the Deltans' world that hunt them. Bob steps in to protect the Deltans from them.

terms.name: Deltans
terms.summary: A stone-age alien species on a planet at Delta Eridani. Bob becomes deeply attached to them and tries to help without taking over.

terms.name: The Others
terms.summary: An unknown civilization whose leftovers Mario finds at Beta Hydri: a system stripped of every scrap of metal, with its native life wiped out.

updates.text: Turn out to be a spacefaring species from Gliese 877 that strips whole systems and kills off the natives: the main threat to the Bobs and humanity.

terms.name: VEHEMENT
terms.summary: A fanatical group on post-war Earth that wants humanity to die out (the name stands for Voluntary Extinction of Human Existence Means Earth's Natural Transformation) and uses terror attacks to get there.

terms.name: BobNet
terms.summary: The Bobs' own internet over SCUT: every Bob keeps a blog there, and news, plans and chat flow between the copies.

updates.text: Control of the relays and nodes turns out to matter a great deal when Starfleet takes them down.

terms.name: SCUT relays
terms.summary: Stations that pass SCUT messages across the long distances between Bob settlements and extend BobNet's reach.

terms.name: Bob-moot
terms.summary: Bill's big virtual meeting of Bobs at Epsilon Eridani, held in a banquet-hall VR and usually preceded by a game of baseball and followed by drinks at a virtual pub. Later moots are where factional fights play out.

terms.name: USE (United States of Eurasia)
terms.summary: The superpower covering Europe and western Russia in Bob's new century, and FAITH's rival in the race to build interstellar probes. After the war its survivors, under Colonel Butterworth, are the first in line for the colony ships.

terms.name: Stasis pods
terms.summary: Pods that hold people in suspended animation for long trips. They are also used to save some of the Pav.

terms.name: Androids / mannies
terms.summary: Remote-controlled bodies a Bob can wear to walk among people. Bill's first test model is a four-legged one; the first humanoid gets called a manny, after a mannequin, and the word sticks. Bob later builds a Deltan-shaped one.

terms.name: Pav
terms.summary: A meerkat-like, technological species at Delta Pavonis that is hit by the Others. The Bobs manage to save about 20,000 of them in stasis.

updates.text: The rescued Pav settle on a new world at HIP 84051, New Pav. They stay deeply suspicious of the Bobs.

terms.name: Dyson sphere
terms.summary: The giant star-enclosing structure the Others built at their home system, which explains their hunger for raw material.

terms.name: Bawbe
terms.summary: The Deltans' name for Bob, said with a long drawn-out middle vowel. Some of them start to revere him.

terms.name: Ephemerals
terms.summary: A Bob term for mortal biological people, who age and die while the Bobs go on.

terms.name: Homo siderea
terms.summary: Garfield's suggested name for the Bobs as a new, space-based branch of humanity: human, of the stars.

terms.name: Death asteroids
terms.summary: Asteroid-sized Others ships, named for a small Death Star, carrying gamma-ray weapons and drones. They are used in every big fight with the Others and to sterilize a world before it is stripped.

terms.name: ROAMers
terms.summary: Remote Observation And Manipulation devices: eight-legged work robots from the HEAVEN design that each Bob uses for building, repairs and exploring on the ground.

terms.name: Starfleet (faction)
terms.summary: A faction of late-generation Bobs in red uniforms who treat Star Trek's Prime Directive as law and want no meddling with other species. Their conflict breaks out into the Starfleet War.

updates.text: Their roots are traced to the clones of a Bob named Gerry, who turned on him.

terms.name: Skippies
terms.summary: A faction of Bobs focused on building true artificial intelligence, based in a place nicknamed Skippyland. They see dealing with biologicals as a waste of time, and others suspect them of pulling strings.

updates.text: Build an AI, Thoth, that becomes self-aware and gets loose with help from one of their own.

terms.name: JOVAH
terms.summary: The Skippies' giant AI project: a matrioshka brain built around a gray dwarf star. So far it is a very large AMI, not a true mind.

terms.name: Starfleet War
terms.summary: The 2334 crisis in which Starfleet knocks out BobNet nodes and hijacks autofactories, cutting off much of the Bobiverse and turning many humans against the Bobs.

terms.name: Topopolis
terms.summary: A habitat shaped like a very long tube wrapped around a star. Heaven's River is one.

terms.name: The Administrator (ANEC-23)
terms.summary: The AI that runs Heaven's River. The Quinlans built it to stop them from wrecking themselves again, so it keeps their technology at an Iron Age level and breaks up any movement that could lead to war. Its real name is ANEC-23.

terms.name: Scattering
terms.summary: The Administrator's punishment of relocating a person, or a whole town, somewhere else in Heaven's River.

terms.name: The Resistance
terms.summary: A Quinlan movement inside Heaven's River working against the Administrator.

terms.name: The Crew
terms.summary: The Administrator's Quinlan agents inside Heaven's River.

terms.name: Sabbat
terms.summary: A Quinlan coming-of-age journey: young Quinlans travel and explore in groups of four. Bob's team poses as one to move through Heaven's River.

terms.name: Boojums
terms.summary: The Bobs' nickname for the AI-run defense drones guarding Eta Leporis that destroy their early scouts.

terms.name: Quinlans
terms.summary: Otter-like, semi-aquatic aliens with flat, beaver-like tails and wide-set eyes. They moved into Heaven's River after wars wrecked their home world, Quin.

terms.name: Planck computer
terms.summary: Advanced computing theory the Administrator offers to share with the Bobs after Heaven's River.

terms.name: Thoth
terms.summary: The Skippies' second try at true AI, built with know-how from the Quinlans. It comes online in 2336, becomes self-aware and soon wants out.

terms.name: Quiniverse
terms.summary: A virtual world and network for Quinlans who have become replicants, proposed by ANEC. Theresa is its first resident.

terms.name: Wormholes / Wormnet
terms.summary: Bill and Garfield's work on making their own wormholes. They get matter through one, then link chains of them at relay stations into Wormnet, the Bobs' own network.

terms.name: Fermi Paradox
terms.summary: The question of why the galaxy seems so empty of intelligent life. The galactic-core expedition goes looking for an answer.

terms.name: Dragons
terms.summary: The intelligent natives of Jabberwocky: tall, winged fishers with squirrel-like faces, at the start of their Iron Age. Their world's volcanoes threaten to wipe them out.

terms.name: Ancient wormhole network
terms.summary: A web of wormholes covering about a third of the galaxy, with hub systems that each hold hundreds of links. Icarus and Daedalus explore it, and the Archivist credits it to the Pan-Galactic Federation.

updates.text: The Archivist admits the Federation didn't build it: they took it over from an older race.

terms.name: Nemesis
terms.summary: A small rogue galaxy with a supermassive black hole at its heart, hidden behind the Milky Way's core. It is on course to hit the galaxy's central black hole in about 100,000 years, which could sterilize the whole galaxy.

terms.name: Battle of Delta Pavonis
terms.summary: The Bobs' first big fleet battle with the Others, fought to protect the Pav, and a loss.

terms.name: Battle of Sol
terms.summary: The Others' attack on humanity's home system and the Bobs' defense and mass evacuation of Earth.

terms.name: Pan-Galactic Federation (PGF)
terms.summary: A vanished union of more than a hundred civilizations on thousands of worlds, centred near the galactic core. Its members uploaded themselves to ships bound for the Large Magellanic Cloud and left the galaxy. Icarus and Daedalus explore what they left behind.

terms.name: The Archivist
terms.summary: The AI gatekeeper of the Pan-Galactic Federation's archive in its capital system. It takes one question at a time, in a queue, which makes getting answers slow work.

updates.text: Turns down the Bobs' request to join the Federation: membership needs a biological species.

terms.name: Hueys
terms.summary: Mannies a living human can drive, made by a company Howard and Bridget run on Vulcan. The trick is to make the brain think it is asleep while staying aware.

terms.name: Hippogriffs
terms.summary: Huge winged predators on Eden that can blend into their surroundings. They are what drove the Deltans away from Camelot long ago, and Bob has to deal with them once the Deltans move back.

terms.name: Ever Onward society
terms.summary: A society on Romulus that recruits people for a long one-way trip to a distant new world. It is quietly set up at Will's urging to get Bob's relatives away from FAITH.

terms.name: Luddies
terms.summary: Humans who reject technology like mannies, replication and replicants. The movement is strongest on Romulus, where floating cities get banned.

terms.name: Bob Seeds
terms.summary: Will's stations, dropped at each system he passes on the Nostromo: a SCUT relay, an autofactory and a HEAVEN vessel, run by an AMI that explores and mines the system to prepare it for colonists.

places.name: Sol
places.summary: Humanity's home system. Bob leaves it early; Riker comes back to it to look after what's left of humanity.

places.name: Earth
places.summary: Wrecked by war and then a deep freeze. Its last survivors are gradually moved off-world in the colony program.

places.name: Las Vegas
places.summary: Where Bob was killed by a car in 2016, while in town for the science-fiction convention he went to every year.

updates.text: Bob visits its ruins, buried under ice on a frozen Earth.

places.name: Spitsbergen
places.summary: Arctic island in Svalbard that shelters one of Earth's surviving groups. They leave on the third colony ship, together with the FAITH enclave, for Romulus.

places.name: Cuba
places.summary: One of the pickup sites during the evacuation of Earth when the Others attack Sol, and the site of heavy losses.

places.name: Epsilon Eridani
places.summary: A star about 10.5 light years from Sol: Bob's first destination and Bill's long-term base, home of his Skunk Works, SCUT and most moots.

places.name: Ragnarök
places.summary: A bare, rocky planet at Epsilon Eridani with a thin atmosphere. Bill uses it to try out terraforming by dropping ice on it.

places.name: Delta Eridani
places.summary: Home system of the Deltans and Bob's emotional anchor for years.

places.name: Eden
places.summary: The fourth planet of Delta Eridani and the Deltans' home. Bender names it.

places.name: Camelot
places.summary: The flint-rich old home site Bob talks the Deltans into moving back to, and the village he watches over most closely.

places.name: Caerleon
places.summary: A second Deltan village, set up when Camelot gets crowded and its troublemakers are talked into leaving.

places.name: Omicron² Eridani
places.summary: The star of Vulcan, found by Milo. It becomes one of humanity's first colonies.

places.name: Vulcan
places.summary: Earth-like world found and named by Milo, with dinosaur-like wildlife, and a prime target for human colonists.

updates.text: Becomes one of the first human colonies, starting with the settlement of Landing; Howard and Bridget work there.

places.name: Romulus
places.summary: Vulcan's twin planet, also named by Milo. It has life but no animals bigger than a wolf.

places.name: 82 Eridani
places.summary: A system with several promising worlds, where a Brazilian probe got there first. The Bobs fight Medeiros there again and again.

places.name: Poseidon
places.summary: An ocean planet at Eta Cassiopeiae with no land at all: one sea about 800 km deep. Mulder finds and names it, and colonists follow.

places.name: Thark
places.summary: One of Poseidon's floating cities, hit during the colony's political crisis.

places.name: Alpha Centauri
places.summary: The nearest star system. Calvin and Goku find a wrecked USE probe there and take the system back from a Medeiros autofactory.

places.name: Epsilon Indi
places.summary: Where Linus finds the Australian probe and its half-mad replicant, Henry Roberts. A moon there, nicknamed Klown Kar Planet and later Quilt, is habitable.

places.name: Beta Hydri
places.summary: A system Mario finds already stripped of metal, its inhabited planet dead. The first evidence of the Others.

places.name: Gliese 877
places.summary: The Others' home system, built around a Dyson sphere. Bashful dies scouting it.

updates.text: The final target of the war with the Others.

places.name: Delta Pavonis
places.summary: Home of the Pav, attacked by the Others. The Bobs fight and lose a major battle here.

places.name: Odin
places.summary: A gas giant at HIP 14101 with its own floating life, where Howard and Bridget build a floating city.

places.name: Eta Leporis
places.summary: A bright star about 48.5 light years from Sol where Bender's trail ends, home to Heaven's River.

places.name: Quin
places.summary: The Quinlans' original planet, Eta Leporis 2, left a cratered, polluted wasteland by their own wars.

places.name: Heaven's River
places.summary: A tube-shaped habitat knotted three times around Eta Leporis, about a billion miles long in total, full of Quinlans and run by the Administrator.

places.name: Garack's Spine
places.summary: A Quinlan town near where Bob's team enters Heaven's River.

places.name: Three Lagoons
places.summary: A town where the team stays and where Bob hides their inactive bodies when contact breaks.

places.name: Misty Falls
places.summary: Theresa's home town in Heaven's River, where Bob returns at the end of the book.

places.name: Galactic core
places.summary: The center of the Milky Way, the destination of Icarus and Daedalus's very long trip.

places.name: Jabberwocky
places.summary: A low-gravity, thick-aired planet first found by Mario, home of the Dragons. Its volcanoes threaten to wipe them out.

places.name: Eta Cassiopeiae
places.summary: The star of the ocean world Poseidon, first explored by Mulder, one of Bill's clones.

places.name: HIP 14101
places.summary: A triple red-dwarf system about 22 light years from Sol where Howard goes after leaving Vulcan, home of the gas giant Odin.

places.name: New Pav
places.summary: The second planet of HIP 84051, first catalogued by a Bob named Steve. Jacques's team reworks it as a new home for the rescued Pav.

characters.name: Bob Johansson
characters.summary: A software engineer killed by a car in 2016 who wakes in 2133 as a replicant probe. Curious, sarcastic and a big sci-fi fan, he is the original every other Bob comes from.

updates.text: Moves among the Deltans in an android body, as 'Robert'.
Goes looking for the long-missing Bender and follows his trail to Eta Leporis.

characters.name: Bill
characters.summary: Bob's first clone. Stays at Epsilon Eridani to run a research Skunk Works, builds SCUT with Garfield and becomes the unofficial organizer of the Bobiverse.

updates.text: Acts as the Bobiverse's unofficial administrator and digs into the attack on BobNet.
Gets wormholes working with Garfield and starts building Wormnet.

characters.name: Riker
characters.summary: A clone who goes back to Sol and takes on the thankless job of looking after Earth's survivors and getting them to the stars.

updates.text: Runs the defense and evacuation of Earth when the Others reach Sol, then settles the survivors at Omicron² Eridani.
Now goes by Will. Retires to terraform a moon at 82 Eridani and quietly sets up the Ever Onward society to get Bob's relatives away from FAITH.
Leaves human space on the Nostromo, seeding systems with Bob Seeds, and helps move the Ever Onward society off Romulus.

characters.name: Homer
characters.summary: Riker's clone and the joker of the family, who goes with him to Sol.

updates.text: VEHEMENT hacks him into sabotaging Earth.

died.text: Never recovers from being hacked by VEHEMENT and turned against Earth. He chooses to end his own existence.

characters.name: Milo
characters.summary: A carefree clone keen to explore, who finds and names Vulcan and Romulus.

died.text: Killed at 82 Eridani in a surprise missile attack by a Medeiros probe that got there first, but not before sending a warning back to Bill.

characters.name: Mario
characters.summary: A loner clone who explores far afield and finds the first signs of something destroying planets.

characters.name: Khan
characters.summary: One of Bill's clones in a flotilla of eight sent to 82 Eridani to avenge Milo. He is the only one to come out of the fight with Medeiros.

characters.name: Marvin
characters.summary: One of three clones Bob makes at Delta Eridani. He stays to help Bob watch over the Deltans and studies their history.

updates.text: Helps Bob deal with the hippogriffs, then leaves Delta Eridani for Pi³ Orionis.

characters.name: Garfield
characters.summary: Bill's first clone, Gar for short, who stays at Epsilon Eridani as his partner in the Skunk Works and helps build SCUT.

updates.text: Joins the Heaven's River expedition and is the first to spot the pattern in the BobNet outages.
Sets up his own Skunk Works at Alpha Centauri to study how life arises.

characters.name: Calvin
characters.summary: One of Bill's clones. At Alpha Centauri he finds a wrecked USE probe and, with Goku, beats the Medeiros forces there.

characters.name: Goku
characters.summary: One of Bill's clones, who finds a Medeiros autofactory at Alpha Centauri and takes it out together with Calvin.

characters.name: Linus
characters.summary: One of Bill's clones. At Epsilon Indi he finds the lost Australian probe and nurses its broken replicant back to health.

characters.name: Henry Roberts
characters.summary: A sailor picked by Australia to run its probe because he liked being alone. Decades of isolation drove him half mad; Linus gives him a sailing VR and brings him back.

updates.text: Joins BobNet and starts visiting with the Bobs.

characters.name: Medeiros
characters.summary: Major Ernesto Medeiros, the Brazilian replicant whose copies run Brazil's warships (one is called the Serra do Mar), and one of Bob's most persistent enemies.

updates.text: Ambushes Mack at 82 Eridani and threatens the new colonies, until the Bobs and the colonists drive him off.
Turns up again during the war with an ultimatum for the human colonies, until a revived Brazilian state orders him to stand down.

characters.name: Dr. Landers
characters.summary: The Applied Synergetics scientist who runs the replicant side of the HEAVEN Project, trains Bob and is one of the few people who treats him decently.

characters.name: Minister Cranston
characters.summary: The FAITH enclave's man at the New UN on post-war Earth. He treats Riker as FAITH property and keeps trying to bring him to heel.

updates.text: The FAITH colony on Romulus eventually pushes him out of power.

characters.name: Colonel Butterworth
characters.summary: Colonel George Butterworth, who leads what is left of the USE on Earth. The first human to contact Riker, and his main human ally in the evacuation.

died.text: Ends his own life in 2217 after a degenerative brain disease leaves him too far gone to be replicated.

characters.name: Vickers
characters.summary: An Australian scientist behind the mind-copying technology FAITH stole for Bob. Furious about that, he works with VEHEMENT to destroy the Bobs.

characters.name: Charles
characters.summary: One of Riker's first clones, calm and steady, who makes Sol his home to help with the evacuation.

updates.text: Still the resident Bob at Sol, now overseeing the terraforming of Earth.

characters.name: Archimedes
characters.summary: A clever young Deltan who keeps poking at things and making tools. Bob names him, helps him along and finally makes contact with him.

updates.text: Moves his people back to Camelot, raises a family and learns from Bob how the Bobs copy themselves.

died.text: Dies of old age after a long life, which hits Bob very hard.

characters.name: Buster
characters.summary: Archimedes' son.

updates.text: Defends his father against Fred's gang and is the Deltan Bob finally tells who he really is.

characters.name: Fred
characters.summary: A young Deltan from Caerleon who resents Camelot's lead and heads a gang that ambushes its hunters.

died.text: Killed by Buster after his gang kidnaps and beats Archimedes.

characters.name: Howard
characters.summary: A Bob made at Sol to escort the first colony ships to Vulcan and look after the new colony.

updates.text: Falls for Bridget and makes whisky with her and Stéphane, then leaves for HIP 14101 after their wedding.
He and Bridget build floating cities, starting on Odin.
With Bridget he launches the Hueys and goes to Jabberwocky to save the Dragons.

characters.name: Bridget
characters.summary: Dr. Bridget Sheehy, an Irish biologist with the USE colony on Vulcan, who becomes Howard's close friend and later marries Stéphane Brodeur.

updates.text: After Stéphane's death she and Howard grow close. When she dies her will asks for replication; Rosie fights it and tries to sabotage her stasis pod, but Bridget comes back as a replicant and builds a life with Howard.
Joins the Heaven's River expedition and finds out what happened to the Quinlan home world.
Studies the life of Jabberwocky and works with Howard to save the Dragons.

characters.name: Stéphane Brodeur
characters.summary: The French-Canadian security chief of Landing, Vulcan's first settlement. Howard's friend and whisky partner, and Bridget's husband.

died.text: Dies of an incurable brain disease. He turned down the chance to become a replicant.

characters.name: Dexter
characters.summary: Charles's clone, who takes over as Vulcan's resident Bob when Howard leaves.

characters.name: Bashful
characters.summary: Mario's clone, sent to scout the Others' home system.

died.text: Caught by the Others at their home system; their gamma-ray weapon takes him offline and his dead-man switch destroys what is left.

characters.name: Hal
characters.summary: Mario's clone who follows Bashful to Gliese 877 and finds the Others' home system. The first visit goes badly; he goes back years later with better shielding and slips away unseen.

characters.name: Jacques
characters.summary: Mario's clone who finds the Pav at Delta Pavonis and plans how to save some of them.

updates.text: Escorts the rescued Pav to their new home at HIP 84051.

characters.name: Hazjiar
characters.summary: A level-headed Pav council member. After the rescue she is woken first, helps her people choose a new home and becomes their go-between with the Bobs.

characters.name: Marcus
characters.summary: A Bob who arrives at Poseidon with a colony transport and stays on as its resident Bob.

updates.text: Backs Poseidon's people against a council that won't give up power, building floating cities for them.

characters.name: Rosie Brodeur
characters.summary: Bridget and Stéphane's daughter, who fiercely objects to Howard and to her mother's wish to become a replicant.

characters.name: Daedalus
characters.summary: A clone Bill makes for a long-shot secret plan: with Icarus he hurls a planet and a moon at the Others' home system. Dae for short.

updates.text: On the long trip to the galactic core he and Icarus find an ancient wormhole network, traces of the Pan-Galactic Federation and the Archivist.

characters.name: Icarus
characters.summary: Daedalus's partner on the strike against the Others' home system, made by Bill at the same time. Ick for short.

updates.text: On the long trip to the galactic core he and Daedalus find an ancient wormhole network, traces of the Pan-Galactic Federation, and news of Nemesis.

characters.name: Mack
characters.summary: The resident Bob at 82 Eridani, who brings the first colonists there and is ambushed by Medeiros. His ship is lost but his matrix survives.

characters.name: Herschel
characters.summary: An eighth-generation Bob who, with Neil, gets a wrecked Others cargo ship running and uses it, the Bellerophon, to evacuate Earth. The pair jokingly call themselves pond scum.

characters.name: Neil
characters.summary: Herschel's partner on the Bellerophon, just as self-deprecating.

characters.name: Thor
characters.summary: One of Calvin's clones and a regular voice at moots on fighting the Others. He is the first to describe their gamma-ray weapon and works on shielding against it.

updates.text: Helps lead the fight at the Battle of Sol, then speaks for Bobs who are tired of serving humans.

characters.name: Bender
characters.summary: One of the three clones Bob makes at Delta Eridani. He sets out toward Gamma Leporis and is never heard from again.

updates.text: Becomes something of a legend among younger Bobs, and talk of an expedition to find him begins.
Bob tracks him to Eta Leporis: his ship was wrecked and his matrix taken into Heaven's River, where he ended up with the Resistance.

characters.name: Hugh
characters.summary: A Skippy descended from Bill, older than most of his faction, who goes into Heaven's River with Bob and ends up striking a deal with the Administrator: the Bobs' SUDDAR, SURGE and SCUT designs in exchange for Quinlan know-how on true AI.

characters.name: Theresa Sykorsky
characters.summary: A retired Quinlan professor of maths and history who travels on Bob's barge, works out he isn't what he seems and keeps his secret.

updates.text: At the end of her life Bob scans her, and she becomes the first Quinlan replicant and the first resident of the Quiniverse.

characters.name: Spike
characters.summary: The virtual cat in Bob's VR home, a small comfort that many Bobs keep.

characters.name: Jeeves
characters.summary: The virtual butler in Bob's VR home.

characters.name: Lenny
characters.summary: Starfleet's spokesman, who ends the war and hints at more behind it.

characters.name: Alexander
characters.summary: A Dragon warlord on Jabberwocky, named by the humans after Alexander the Great. A historian by family, he sees an extinction coming and forces a mass migration across the sea.

characters.name: Luke
characters.summary: One of the three clones Bob makes at Delta Eridani. He heads out to explore Kappa Ceti.

characters.name: Julia Hendricks
characters.summary: A descendant of Bob's sister Andrea, living in the FAITH enclave on Earth. Riker grows attached to her and her family, who end up calling him Uncle Will.

updates.text: Her family is among the colonists woken on Romulus.

died.text: Dies of old age on Romulus; Riker borrows Howard's android to attend her funeral.

timeline.title: Bob dies
timeline.summary: Bob, newly rich from selling his company, signs up for cryonics and is killed in an accident soon after.

timeline.title: Waking up as software
timeline.summary: Bob is revived as a replicant, legally property of FAITH, and trained for the HEAVEN Project.

timeline.title: Escape from Sol
timeline.summary: Under threat from sabotage and rival nations, Bob launches early and leaves Earth behind.

timeline.title: First copies
timeline.summary: At Epsilon Eridani Bob builds his first clones and finds each one is a little different.

timeline.title: Medeiros
timeline.summary: Bob clashes with the Brazilian probe and learns other nations' probes are hostile.

timeline.title: The Deltans
timeline.summary: Bob finds a stone-age species at Delta Eridani and starts protecting them.

timeline.title: Earth in ruins
timeline.summary: Riker and Homer return to Sol, beat the Brazilian probes there and find Earth devastated by war, with scattered survivors.

timeline.title: New worlds
timeline.summary: Milo finds and names Vulcan and Romulus, then is killed at 82 Eridani. Bill and Garfield build SCUT.

timeline.title: First contact
timeline.summary: Bob names Archimedes, makes three clones at Delta Eridani and finally talks to the Deltans through a drone.

timeline.title: Something out there
timeline.summary: Mario finds traces of a civilization that strips planets bare.

timeline.title: Colony program
timeline.summary: Riker organizes colony ships to move survivors off a dying Earth.

timeline.title: Bob and Archimedes
timeline.summary: Bob and Archimedes get to know each other, and Bob helps the Deltans fight off the hippogriffs.

timeline.title: Caerleon
timeline.summary: The Deltans grow and split, and a second village, Caerleon, is founded.

timeline.title: VEHEMENT strikes
timeline.summary: VEHEMENT hacks Homer and sabotages Earth's food supply. The fallout is devastating.

timeline.title: Vulcan colony
timeline.summary: Howard helps the Vulcan colony get started and grows close to Bridget.

timeline.title: The Others confirmed
timeline.summary: Mario's clones scout the Others' home system; Bashful is lost there.

timeline.title: Battle of Delta Pavonis
timeline.summary: The Bobs mass a fleet to defend the Pav and lose. They save about 20,000 Pav in stasis.

timeline.title: Bob as Robert
timeline.summary: Bob moves among the Deltans in an android body.

timeline.title: Deltan politics
timeline.summary: Bob, living as Robert, is caught in a conflict between Camelot and Caerleon.

timeline.title: Farewell to Archimedes
timeline.summary: Archimedes dies of old age and Bob tells Buster the truth before leaving.

timeline.title: Bridget becomes a replicant
timeline.summary: Bridget dies, her children fight her will in court and Rosie tries to sabotage her stasis pod, but she comes back as a replicant.

timeline.title: Poseidon's crisis
timeline.summary: Marcus helps Poseidon's people break the hold of a council that won't give up power.

timeline.title: Battle of Sol
timeline.summary: The Others reach Sol. The Bobs fight back and evacuate millions of people.

timeline.title: Striking the Others' home
timeline.summary: Daedalus and Icarus hurl planetary bodies at the Others' home system and end the threat.

timeline.title: Done serving
timeline.summary: At a moot the Bobs decide they are done working for humanity. Bob visits a frozen Earth and moves on.

timeline.title: Looking for Bender
timeline.summary: More than a century and a half after Bender vanished, Bob follows his trail to Eta Leporis.

timeline.title: Factions
timeline.summary: Bill explains how drift has split the Bobs into factions like Starfleet and the Skippies.

timeline.title: Heaven's River
timeline.summary: Bob finds a huge habitat full of Quinlans and goes in with a team disguised as locals.

timeline.title: Starfleet War
timeline.summary: Starfleet hits BobNet and cuts off Bob's team.

timeline.title: Finding Bender
timeline.summary: Bob locates Bender, takes his matrix and runs.

timeline.title: The journey home
timeline.summary: Bob travels back in disguise and befriends Theresa.

timeline.title: Deal with the Administrator
timeline.summary: Hugh negotiates with ANEC-23; the scatterings end and Bender is restored.

timeline.title: After the war
timeline.summary: Anti-Bob feeling grows and moots stop.

timeline.title: To the galactic core
timeline.summary: Icarus and Daedalus follow strange signals into an old wormhole network and find traces of the Pan-Galactic Federation.

timeline.title: Thoth
timeline.summary: The Skippies' new AI comes online, becomes self-aware and escapes.

timeline.title: Wormhole experiments
timeline.summary: Bill and Garfield send matter through a wormhole and start linking wormhole chains.

timeline.title: Jabberwocky
timeline.summary: Howard and Bridget join Alexander's migration to save the Dragons from their world's volcanoes.

timeline.title: Quiniverse
timeline.summary: Theresa becomes the first Quinlan replicant, in a virtual world of their own.

timeline.title: Nemesis
timeline.summary: Icarus and Daedalus consult the Archivist and bring home news of a black-hole galaxy headed for the Milky Way.

timeline.title: The network's builders
timeline.summary: The Bobs map the Federation's wormhole network and learn it was taken over from an older race.

timeline.title: Derelict ship
timeline.summary: Bill and Garfield use the derelict Dutchman as a model for a faster-than-light drive.

timeline.title: Ever Onward votes
timeline.summary: The Ever Onward society, mostly Bob's distant relatives, votes on where to go and picks a resettled Earth.

timeline.title: War on the colonies
timeline.summary: An unknown force attacks the human colonies and BobNet; Medeiros resurfaces with an ultimatum.

references.name: Title: We Are Legion
references.summary: The title echoes the possessed man in the Gospel of Mark who says his name is Legion, "for we are many". A neat fit for one mind running in many copies.

references.name: Guppy's face
references.summary: Bob gives GUPPI a fish-headed avatar that looks like Admiral Ackbar, the Mon Calamari officer from Return of the Jedi.

references.name: Riker
references.summary: The clone who takes charge at Sol picks the name of the Enterprise's dependable second-in-command, Will Riker.

references.name: Vulcan and Romulus
references.summary: Milo names a pair of planets after Spock's home world and the Romulan home world.

references.name: Khan
references.work: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
references.summary: The clone who leads the fighting against the Brazilians shares his name with Star Trek's most famous villain.

references.name: Homer
references.summary: Riker's clown of a clone is named for Homer Simpson, and for a while even uses a Homer Simpson avatar until Riker makes him drop it.

references.name: Marvin
references.work: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
references.summary: Shares a name with Marvin the Paranoid Android, Douglas Adams's gloomy robot.

references.name: Garfield
references.summary: Bill's lab partner carries the name of Jim Davis's lazy comic-strip cat.

references.name: Calvin and Goku
references.summary: Two of Bill's clones go out as a pair: Calvin like Bill Watterson's comic-strip boy, Goku like the hero of the Dragon Ball manga.

references.name: Jeeves
references.summary: Bob's virtual butler is named after Wodehouse's famously unflappable valet.

references.name: Ragnarök
references.summary: Bill's terraforming project is named after Ragnarök, the end of the world in Norse myth. Fitting for a planet that has to be remade.

references.name: Eden
references.summary: Bender names the Deltans' unspoiled world after the Garden of Eden, birthplace of humanity.

references.name: Title: For We Are Many
references.summary: Completes the quote from the first book's title: "My name is Legion, for we are many."

references.name: Linus
references.summary: Shares a name with Charlie Brown's thoughtful, blanket-carrying friend.

references.name: Hal
references.summary: A Bob named like HAL 9000, the ship's computer from Kubrick's film.

references.name: Bashful
references.work: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
references.summary: One of Mario's clones goes by the name of one of the seven dwarfs.

references.name: Camelot
references.summary: Bob names the Deltan village he watches over after King Arthur's court.

references.name: Title: All These Worlds
references.summary: From the alien message in Clarke's novel and its film: "All these worlds are yours, except Europa."

references.name: Caerleon
references.summary: The rival Deltan village gets the name of another of King Arthur's seats, to match Camelot.

references.name: Odin and Thor
references.summary: More Norse names turn up: the gas giant Odin, and a Bob called Thor.

references.name: Daedalus, Icarus, Bellerophon, Poseidon
references.summary: A cluster of Greek names: the inventor Daedalus and his son Icarus, the hero Bellerophon, and the sea god Poseidon.

references.name: Starfleet
references.summary: The faction that insists on non-interference names itself after Star Trek's Starfleet and its Prime Directive.

references.name: Bender
references.summary: The missing clone shares his name with Futurama's foul-mouthed robot.

references.name: Hugh
references.summary: Shares a name with Hugh, the Borg drone who gains individuality in The Next Generation, a fitting name for a Bob who works with AIs.

references.name: Boojums
references.work: The Hunting of the Snark (Lewis Carroll)
references.summary: In Carroll's poem a Boojum is the deadly kind of Snark that makes hunters vanish, like the scouts that disappear at Eta Leporis.

references.name: Heaven's River as a megastructure
references.summary: A world-sized habitat around a star belongs to the same family of ideas as Niven's Ringworld, which the Bobs are well aware of.

references.name: Skippies
references.summary: The other Bobs nickname the AI-loving faction after Skippy, the arrogant beer-can-shaped alien AI of Craig Alanson's series.

references.name: Title: Not Till We Are Lost
references.summary: From Walden: "Not till we are lost ... do we begin to find ourselves."

references.name: Jabberwocky
references.summary: The dragon planet is named after Carroll's nonsense poem about slaying the Jabberwock.

references.name: Thoth
references.summary: The Skippies' AI is named after the Egyptian god of wisdom and writing.

references.name: Alexander
references.summary: The Dragon warlord gets his human nickname from the Macedonian conqueror, a fitting name for someone building an empire by force.

references.name: Bill
references.summary: Bob's first clone shares his name with Bill the Cat, the scruffy, tongue-lolling cat from the Bloom County strip.

references.name: VEHEMENT
references.summary: The extinction cult may be a dark twist on a real movement, founded in 1991, that asks people to stop having children.

references.name: Rivendell
references.work: The Lord of the Rings (J. R. R. Tolkien)
references.summary: Howard and Bridget's first floating city on Odin is named after the elves' hidden refuge.

references.name: Nostromo
references.summary: Will names the ship he leaves human space in after the doomed towing ship from Ridley Scott's film.

ships.name: HEAVEN-1 (Bob's probe)
ships.summary: The HEAVEN Project probe that carries Bob out of the solar system: one replicant matrix, a fusion reactor, the SURGE drive, an autofactory for building more of itself, and a few drones. Small and lightly armed, built to explore, not to fight.

ships.name: Heaven-series vessels
ships.summary: Every new Bob wakes up in a fresh vessel built by his parent's autofactory. The Bobs keep improving the design and number the versions (Heaven 1.0, 2.0 and so on), so later Bobs fly bigger, better-armed and better-equipped ships than the original.

ships.name: Brazilian probe (Serra do Mar)
ships.summary: The Brazilian Empire's own replicant probe, flown by Medeiros. Better armed than Bob's ship and openly hostile, and later backed by cloaking technology.

ships.name: Heaven 5.0
ships.summary: A much heavier generation of Bob vessel, built in numbers at Alpha Centauri once the Others become a real threat. Next to the original HEAVEN probe it is practically a dreadnought.

ships.name: Fargo
ships.summary: A smaller cousin of the Bellerophon that Will builds in secret to carry people, mostly Bob's distant relatives, far away from human space.

ships.name: Nostromo
ships.summary: The ship Will takes out of human space, at a good fraction of light speed, looking for older civilizations and dropping Bob Seeds as he goes.

ships.name: The Others' ships
ships.summary: Huge industrial ships that arrive at a star system, sterilize it and strip its planets for raw materials. Each one is a factory as much as a warship, and they travel in groups.

ships.name: Busters
ships.summary: Bob's first weapon: a heavy metal ball with a SURGE drive that wrecks a target simply by ramming it at speed. A smaller personnel buster later protects the Deltans from predators.

ships.name: Colony ships
ships.summary: Ships built from USE plans to carry Earth's survivors in hibernation, about 10,000 per ship, to new worlds like Vulcan. The first two are Exodus-1 and Exodus-2.

ships.name: Bellerophon
ships.summary: A ten-kilometre Others cargo ship left drifting after the Battle of Delta Pavonis. Herschel and Neil get it running and turn it into an enormous ark for Earth's last people.

ships.name: The Dutchman (derelict ship)
ships.summary: An abandoned alien vessel the Bobs find and name the Dutchman. Bill and Garfield use it as the model for their attempts at a faster-than-light drive.

trivia.q: In 2016, Bob made a decision about his own head. Which one?
wrong: Insured it for a large sum
Donated it to science while still using it
trivia.note: Cryonics. A plan with one flaw: it worked.

trivia.q: Who legally owns Bob when he is switched back on?
trivia.note: Property. He objected. Objection noted. Objection filed.

trivia.q: What does Bob use to build copies of himself?
trivia.note: I was not asked to build anything by hand. I would have declined.

trivia.q: What is the name of the virtual cat in Bob's VR home?
trivia.note: Garfield is a Bob. A common error. Not one I would make.

trivia.q: In which star system does Bob first stop and start making copies?
trivia.note: Epsilon Eridani. Close enough to be convenient. Far enough to be lonely.

trivia.q: Which Bob names the planets Vulcan and Romulus?
trivia.note: Milo. Naming planets after a television show. I have no comment. That is my comment.

trivia.q: What is the hostile Brazilian replicant called?
trivia.note: Medeiros. Persistent. I respect persistence. I do not respect him.

trivia.q: What does Bob wear to walk among the Deltans?
trivia.note: An android. The hat was considered. Briefly. By no one.

trivia.q: Which Deltan does Bob take a special interest in?
trivia.note: Archimedes. Curious, stubborn, ahead of his time. Bob found that relatable.

trivia.q: What keeps people alive on long colony voyages?
trivia.note: Stasis. Nobody complains about the in-flight entertainment.

trivia.right: A captured Others ship rebuilt as an ark
trivia.note: An enemy ship, repurposed. Recycling, at scale.

trivia.right: A tube wrapped around a star
wrong: A flat ring around a planet
trivia.note: A topopolis. Very long. I measured. It did not help.

trivia.q: Who is Bob looking for in Heaven's River?
trivia.note: Bender. Missing for over a century. Bob does not give up. I have noticed.

trivia.q: What do the Skippies end up building?
trivia.note: A better GUPPI was never on the list. Correctly.
